office_does: Douglas County's three commissioners adopt the county budget and property-tax levies, set land-use rules for the unincorporated county, and oversee roads, facilities and county departments.
race_blurb: Two-term incumbent Marc Straub of Orondo faces Michael S. Lesky, who states an Independent preference and filed no voters' guide statement. Lesky drew 710 votes to Straub's 2,583 in the District 3 primary; the whole county votes in the general.

candidates.summary: District 3 commissioner since his 2018 election and former 17-year CEO of Building North Central Washington, running for a third term on economic development, infrastructure upkeep and fiscal restraint.
highlights: First elected in 2018 with 64.8% and re-elected unopposed in 2022 [S3][S4]
Says the county 'should never take a state-plus-one approach' to regulation [S2]
Pledges to prioritize funding for the Sheriff's office, emergency services and first responders [S2]
Chaired the board in 2022 when commissioners set up an in-house public defender's office [S7]; said the Wenatchi Landing development would create hundreds of jobs [S8]
Endorsed by the Douglas County Republican Central Committee and retired Sheriff Kevin Morris [S2]

experience.basis: Eight-year incumbent and board chair who runs on 'experience matters' and continuing work already in motion.

spending.basis: Platform of limited government, a balanced budget prioritizing core functions, and 'resisting waste'; stated in his own campaign materials.

safety.basis: Campaign priority on funding the Sheriff's office and first responders; no prevention or diversion program proposals.

candidates.summary: Candidate with an Orondo mailing address who prefers the Independent Party; he filed no voters' guide statement, reports no campaign activity to the PDC, and no public platform was found.
highlights: Received 710 of 3,308 votes (21.5%) in the District 3 primary [S3]
Filed no voters' guide statement; his PDC registration shows no contributions or spending [S1][S4]
